messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Canary rollout for model 'rw-small-v2-quant' is seeing elevated 5xx rates and a large number of sticky fallbacks to us-west. Triggered by policy mismatch at 18:20 UTC.

sasha: oncall here, looking now. can someone paste the canary config? i want to see fallback policy.

mike: pasting snippet from the rollout manifest:
```
canary:
  percent: 10
  sticky_fallback: true
  fallback_policy:
    primary_region: eu-central-1
    fallback_region: us-west-2
    variant: v1-fp16
```

mike: note the fallback variant is v1-fp16 (older model). suspect requests are being routed to that variant when the canary fails which is causing tokenization/formatting errors.

jia: i see errors in the logs where client requests expect 'v2-quant' token ids; upstream returned unknown tokens -> 500s. sample log:
`[18:22:11] req_id=abc123 model_mismatch expected=rw-small-v2-quant served=rw-small-v1-fp16`

ops-oncall: this is causing user-visible failures for some customers in EU. traffic that should have been pinned to canary is falling back and getting sticky mapped to us-west, adding latency and some retry storms.

sasha: immediate mitigations: 1) pause the rollout 2) disable sticky_fallback 3) set fallback_region to eu-central-1 only 4) roll back canary if errors continue. i'll start 1 and 2 now.

deploy-bot: deploy start: update rollout config by sasha at 18:27 UTC

mike: to disable sticky we need to update the routing policy key `sticky_fallback` -> false and clear any sticky cookies for active sessions. command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --rollout-id=rl-789 --set sticky_fallback=false
redwoodctl sessions flush --scope=canary
```

elaine-support: i am starting outreach to affected customers. initial estimate: ~12 orgs hit with >10% error rate during the spike. opening a banner on status site now.

jia: paused the rollout (api call returned 200). also changed fallback_region to eu-central-1 only. monitoring metrics now.

sasha: good. mike, can you confirm whether the mismatch was due to a bad variant label in the canary config or a kernel selection issue in the runtime?

mike: digging: rollout manifest referenced `variant: v1-fp16` as the fallback. runtime kernel selection was fine for v1-fp16, but our tokenizer mapping between v2-quant and v1-fp16 differs. so requests that fell back got misinterpreted. root cause is config-level variant mismatch.

ops-oncall: are there any customers still getting 5xxs after the disabling of sticky fallbacks?

elaine-support: errors dropped sharply after 18:32 UTC. a couple of customers still reporting intermittent timeouts, likely due to retry cascades. i'm sending targeted follow-ups.

deploy-bot: deploy success: routing update finished 18:31 UTC

mike: cleared session sticky keys for the canary group at 18:33 UTC. verified that subsequent requests hitting fallback_region eu-central-1 only and using compatible variant v2-quant.

sasha: keeping rollout paused. setting a temporary guard: require variant compatibility check before any canary >0%. i'll push a waffle flag for rollout validation.

jia: added a pre-rollout validator (checks tokenizer compatibility, model signature) and enabled for this team. patch id: PR-4321. recommend postmortem to make this mandatory.

ops-oncall: customer impact summary for incident channel and oncall page: 12 customers affected, highest error rate window 18:20-18:32 UTC, majority recovered by 18:34 UTC. no SLOs breached beyond 5-minute blip but multiple support tickets opened.

sasha: handoff: i'm leaving shift at 19:00 UTC. jia will take oncall and coordinate postmortem + follow-ups. tagging @jia.

jia: acknowledged — taking over oncall. i'll coordinate postmortem and the customer comms draft with elaine.

elaine-support: drafting status update: "Investigating an issue where canary fallbacks routed to an incompatible model variant, causing elevated errors for some EU customers. Rollout paused and routing policy adjusted. Customers impacted are being contacted." will post in 10.

mike: short-term code fix: add a validation step in rollout controller to compare tokenizer hashes between primary and fallback variants. failing that, controller rejects the rollout with error. patch in progress.

sasha: great. next actions: (1) jia + mike produce postmortem, include timeline + config diff (2) engineering to add rollout-blocker tests for variant compatibility (3) product ops to review canary policy defaults (sticky_fallback should be opt-in with validator on)

jia: assigning ownership: postmortem owner = jia, eng owner = mike, support comms = elaine. ETA for postmortem 48h.

incident-bot: incident-timeline recorded, severity set to P2, linked to runbook 'canary-fallback-mismatch'.

sasha: thanks team. i'll follow up in the postmortem thread after handoff. :thumbsup:

elaine-support: support notes: sent personalized messages to top 5 affected customers; created follow-ups for the rest.

mike: monitoring shows stable error rate now, no new spikes for 25m. keeping a 1hr elevated monitor window.

jia: taking over. continuing monitoring and will schedule the postmortem meeting. closing this thread when postmortem is created.
summary: Canary rollout hit by incompatible fallback variant + sticky fallback. Rollout paused, sticky disabled, sessions flushed, fallback region constrained. 12 customers impacted briefly. Postmortem triaged and oncall handoff completed.
